title: Quantization Profile Console UX flow (route-level toggle, warnings, confirmation, changelog)
creator: Dylan Brooks
description: Design the Redwood Console route-level quantization profile enablement flow: placement in the UI, selection & toggle behavior, confirmation modal, compatibility/quality warnings, and change history visibility. This ticket is focused on UX/IA and copy guidance (not API implementation).
body:
## Background
We are launching an opt-in Quantization Profile Library. Customers can enable a specific quantization profile per route (and optionally scope by region/deployment tier via existing route policy controls). Enabling can change output quality/latency characteristics and has strict compatibility constraints (model variant, GPU SKU class, max context regime). We must make the action deliberate, reversible, auditable, and understandable.

This ticket covers the Console UX flow for:
- Where the control lives in Route settings
- How users pick a profile (and how we represent “default/off”)
- Confirmation modal (risk + scope clarity)
- Warnings and compatibility checks (blocking vs non-blocking)
- Changelog/audit surfacing (who/what/when)

## Goals
1) Make it hard to accidentally enable quantization (explicit intent + confirmation).
2) Prevent invalid configurations (incompatible profile/model/hardware) with clear remediation.
3) Make rollback obvious (one click disable, plus visibility of kill-switch impact).
4) Make the action auditable for enterprise (change history + link to audit export).

## Non-goals
- Designing automated “recommended profile” or silent upgrades (out of scope for v1).
- Designing global tenant defaults (ADR decision is route-level only).
- Full dashboard design (covered elsewhere), except what we surface inline at decision time.

---

## Proposed information architecture / placement
### Location
Console → **Routes** → select route → **Settings** tab (existing) → section: **Performance & Cost** (new) → card: **Quantization profiles (Beta)**

Rationale:
- Route is the unit of enablement (ADR-0137). Putting the control at route settings matches mental model and avoids surprising tenant-wide changes.
- “Performance & Cost” framing aligns with why users want this (cost/token, throughput).

### Card layout (collapsed / expanded)
**Collapsed state** (default):
- Title: Quantization profiles (Beta)
- Status pill: “Off (default precision)” OR “On: <profile name>” OR “Applied with fallbacks” (see below)
- Subtext: “Reduce cost by enabling an approved quantization profile for this route.”
- CTA: “Configure”

**Expanded state**:
1) **Enablement**
   - Toggle: Off/On (explicit)
   - When Off: profile selector disabled; shows “Using default runtime precision.”
2) **Profile selector** (only active if On)
   - Dropdown listing compatible profiles for the route’s model variant (server-filtered)
   - Option “Default (no profile)” shown but only selectable when toggle is Off to avoid ambiguous states
   - Each option shows: profile name, precision summary, status tag (Stable/Experimental/Deprecated), and “Last updated”
3) **Compatibility status**
   - Inline badge: Compatible / Incompatible / Unknown (loading)
   - “View details” expander: GPU classes supported, max context constraints, known caveats
4) **Safety / quality guidance**
   - Inline callout: “Run evals before broad rollout” with link to eval playbook
   - Optional “Canary” affordance is handled by existing rollout tooling; here we provide a link + copy, not new controls

---

## Interaction design details
### Default state
- Feature flag off / not allowlisted:
  - Hide entire card (preferred) OR show read-only “Contact support to enable Beta” depending on PM preference.
  - Decision: hide by default for GA behind allowlist; show read-only for internal/staff + design partners.

- Feature flag on + allowlisted:
  - Card visible.
  - Toggle defaults to Off.
  - Existing route behavior is unchanged unless user explicitly turns On and confirms.

### Enabling flow (happy path)
1) User opens route settings → Quantization profiles card.
2) User toggles On.
3) Profile dropdown becomes active; user selects a profile.
4) Console calls “validate/preview” endpoint:
   - Returns compatibility + warnings + estimated impact (if available).
5) User clicks “Save”.
6) **Confirmation modal** (required) appears.
7) User confirms (type-to-confirm only for high risk cases; see below) → changes are saved.
8) Success toast includes: “Quantization enabled: <profile>” + “View change log”.

### Confirmation modal spec
**Title:** Enable quantization profile for this route?

**Body (always shown):**
- Route: <route name> (with environment)
- Model: <model_id / variant>
- Selected profile: <profile name> + precision summary
- Scope: “Applies to requests served by this route. If the profile is incompatible at runtime, requests will fall back to baseline precision.”

**Warnings section (conditional):**
- If profile status = Experimental: show yellow warning “Experimental: may change or be deprecated. Validate quality before production rollout.”
- If profile has known caveats (e.g., max context): show warning with concrete constraint.
- If we detect higher latency risk (from perf suite metadata): show “May increase tail latency for long contexts.”

**Quality guidance (always):**
- Checkbox: “I understand this can change output quality and I will evaluate before broad rollout.” (required)
- Link: “Route-level quantization eval playbook”

**Actions:**
- Primary: “Enable profile”
- Secondary: “Cancel”

**Escalation / high-risk confirmation:**
Require type-to-confirm (“ENABLE”) if ANY of:
- Profile marked Experimental AND route environment = Production
- Profile is Deprecated (we should strongly discourage enabling deprecated; ideally block)
- Known caveat severity = High (e.g., “may produce invalid JSON” for structured output routes)

### Disabling / rollback flow
- Toggle Off → Save
- No confirmation modal required (keep rollback fast), but show a small non-blocking prompt: “Disable quantization now? This will revert to default precision.”
- Success toast: “Quantization disabled. Route reverted to default precision.”

### Incompatibility behavior (UX)
We must distinguish between:
1) **Cannot be enabled (hard block)**: profile is incompatible with the route’s model variant (or policy constraints known at config time).
2) **May fall back (runtime)**: profile is generally compatible, but runtime may fall back in specific conditions (e.g., GPU class mismatch due to capacity routing; max context exceeded).

**Hard block behavior (config-time):**
- Save disabled.
- Inline error: “Incompatible with this route’s model/hardware policy.”
- Provide remediation:
  - “Choose a different profile”
  - “Change route hardware tier / region constraints” (link to routing policy section)
  - “Contact support”

**Runtime fallback (non-blocking):**
- Allow save.
- Show info callout: “Some requests may fall back to baseline precision if the profile can’t be applied. Monitor fallback rate.” Link to dashboard panel.

### Kill-switch / platform override visibility
If global kill-switch is active or tenant-level override disables profiles:
- Show prominent banner in the card:
  - “Quantization profiles are currently disabled by your organization or Redwood due to an incident. Existing settings are preserved but not applied.”
- Controls become read-only (disabled) with tooltip explaining why.

---

## Changelog / audit visibility
### Where it shows
Routes → route details → **Change history** (existing) + filter “Quantization”

### What we show
For each event:
- Timestamp
- Actor (user/service) + auth method (SSO if available)
- Action: Enabled / Disabled / Profile changed
- Diff: {old_profile_ref → new_profile_ref} and {old_enabled → new_enabled}
- Environment + route id
- Optional: validation outcome at time of change (Compatible / Allowed with fallback risk)

### Link-out
- “Export audit logs” link (if customer has Audit Log Export enabled)
- For enterprise: show the event name/ID matching the audit log schema so compliance teams can correlate.

---

## Copy guidelines (draft)
- Use “Quantization profile” consistently (avoid “quant mode”).
- Avoid implying quality is guaranteed. Preferred language:
  - “Designed to reduce cost while preserving quality”
  - “May change outputs; evaluate before production rollout”
- “Fallback” should be explained as safety behavior, not as silent success.

---

## Deliverables
- Updated route settings IA + wireframes for card states
- Confirmation modal wireframe + copy variants (prod vs non-prod)
- Changelog filter / row spec
- Error and warning message list (compatibility, kill-switch, deprecated)

Figma: (placeholder) https://figma.redwoodinference.com/file/DES-418-quant-profile-route-toggle

---

## Open questions
1) Should we show the card for non-allowlisted users as a teaser (“Request access”) or hide entirely? (PM to decide; current recommendation: hide to reduce confusion.)
2) Do we require confirmation modal on profile change (On → different profile) in addition to first enable? Recommendation: yes in production, no in staging.
3) Should deprecated profiles be selectable? Recommendation: do not allow enabling; if already enabled, show “Deprecated” + nudge to migrate.
4) Do we surface estimated savings inline (from benchmark lab) or only in a linked dashboard? Recommendation: show a small “Expected cost reduction: ~X–Y% (varies)” when we have metadata; otherwise omit.

## References
- PRD: PRD Quantization Profile Library (opt-in)
- ADR: ADR-0137 Route-level quantization profile enablement
- Serving standard: Quantization profile compatibility and fallbacks
- Support: rollback procedure for quantization profiles
acceptance_criteria:
1) Route settings placement and section/card spec are documented (collapsed + expanded states).
2) Confirmation modal requirements are defined (when required, required checkbox, type-to-confirm conditions).
3) Compatibility UX is defined with clear hard-block vs runtime-fallback behaviors and remediation copy.
4) Kill-switch/override read-only behavior is specified.
5) Change history/audit visibility requirements are specified (fields, filter, diff).
6) Figma link or equivalent design artifact is attached and shared with Console eng + PM for implementation.

activity_log: 2025-02-03 (Dylan Brooks): Created ticket after Console UX review kickoff; requested dedicated flow for confirmation + audit visibility.
2025-02-07 (Tessa Morgan): Proposed IA: Route Settings → Performance & Cost → Quantization profiles card. Added first draft modal + warning taxonomy.
2025-02-12 (Kenji Nakamura): Reviewed control placement + interaction details; suggested type-to-confirm for Experimental + prod only; aligned with rollout controls elsewhere.
2025-02-18 (Chloe Martin): Confirmed backend can provide validate/preview endpoint for compatibility + warnings; asked for explicit hard-block vs fallback UX distinctions.
2025-02-24 (Jada Williams): Requested change history diff fields + filter; noted enterprise customers need actor + route identifiers visible and exportable.
2025-03-03 (Marissa Cole): PM sign-off on: no global defaults; confirmation required on enable; disable should be one-step rollback. Requested allowlist behavior to be “hidden by default”.
2025-03-10 (Dylan Brooks): Final stakeholder sign-off captured; ready for ENG-5818 implementation.
comments: Tessa Morgan (2025-02-07): Drafted a card-based UI so we don’t bury this behind advanced settings. Key is making the action deliberate without making rollback slow. Proposed: confirmation modal on enable + profile change in prod, but not on disable.

Kenji Nakamura (2025-02-12): +1 on confirmation modal. For type-to-confirm, keep it limited—otherwise users will bypass without reading. Suggest only when Experimental+Prod or if the profile contains a high severity caveat.

Chloe Martin (2025-02-18): Engineering note: we can return structured warnings (severity/info/warn/block) from the preview endpoint. If design can map these to UI patterns, it’ll simplify the implementation.

Jada Williams (2025-02-24): Audit/Change history: we need a human-readable diff and a stable event name/id. Please ensure copy doesn’t imply audit log export is always available (some tiers won’t have it).
Marissa Cole (2025-03-03): PM decision: hide the card for users not allowlisted for Beta (avoid confusion/support load). For design partners, show the card with a “Beta” label.
Dylan Brooks (2025-03-10): Approved. Please ensure the success toast links to change history; support teams will use it for quick triage.
